transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-14 16:30 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes (scheduled)
- Attendees: Jasmine Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Leah Kim (Redwood CSM), Evelyn Moore (CISO, Silverpine), Tom Nguyen (Head of Platform), Priya Shah (DevOps), Raj Patel (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Silverpine is evaluating options between Redwood Hosted and Dedicated, with potential Private deployment later. Primary concerns: KMS integration and customer-managed keys, SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning, RBAC and granular audit logs, data residency and retention policies, and latency/cost trade-offs for high-throughput batch inference. They requested artifacts (SOC2/ISO docs) and a Dedicated architecture diagram plus a small benchmark run.

Topics: SOC2 / ISO status; encryption at rest / KMS; SSO / SAML + SCIM; RBAC and tenant isolation; audit log format and retention; network/VPC options and private deployment; cost/latency tradeoffs; next steps.

[00:00] Jasmine Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jasmine from redwood, i'm the account owner, i'll hand it to marco to kick off on the technical side in a second — but first quick intros?
[00:12] Evelyn Moore: evelyn, ciso at silverpine, i've got tom and priya and raj on the line as well. we're leading security and compliance evaluation for our AI platform initiatives.
[00:22] Tom Nguyen: tom, head of platform, focused on infra and latency SLA.
[00:28] Priya Shah: priya, devops, i'll be hands-on if we run any pilots.
[00:33] Marco Diaz: great — marco, solutions engineer at redwood. quick agenda: we want to understand your requirements around encryption/kms, sso, audit logs, and then map hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private) to those needs. also outline what artifacts we can share.

[00:50] Jasmine Patel: quick ask from our side — timeline and success criteria? when do you need a vendor decision?
[00:56] Evelyn Moore: timeline is Q3 procurement ideally — we have internal pilots in june, decision by end of july. success is: vendor must pass our security checklist including SOC2, offer customer-managed KMS or equivalent, SSO/SAML with SCIM, RBAC scoping per team, and auditability for regulatory audits.

[01:20] Marco Diaz: understood. on SOC2 — redwood is SOC2 Type II, and we also have ISO27001 in progress, i can send certs. for KMS, we support both customer-managed keys in KMS for private deployments and a bring-your-own-key option for Dedicated + Private; Hosted also supports envelope encryption with customer-provided keys via our KMS integration for enterprise plans.

[01:45] Evelyn Moore: pause — can you explain the difference in practice? we need to ensure zero-access to plaintext and that keys are managed in our cloud.
[01:54] Marco Diaz: yes — for customer-managed keys in the private model, the control plane runs in your VPC and keys never leave your KMS — redwood's inference runtime performs decryption inside customer network; for Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS (IAM roles) so decryption happens on the dedicated hosts with strict IAM. Hosted with CMKs is possible but has some restrictions around rotation and cross-account policies — i'll detail that in the doc.

[02:20] Tom Nguyen: are there any latencies introduced by envelope encryption or KMS calls per token? that's a big one for us.
[02:30] Marco Diaz: good question. we cache decrypted model artifacts and use envelope keys — the per-request KMS exchange is minimized; most KMS calls occur at startup or key rotation. for token-level operations there is negligible added latency. in benchmarks we saw <10ms overhead for key ops in dedicated deployments, but host-specific. we can run a bench with your dataset.

[02:58] Priya Shah: ok, please add that to the bench scope — and also how we can test prefix/KV cache behavior because our workload has many similar prompts.

[03:10] Jasmine Patel: noted — marco will share a benchmark plan. next, SSO?

[03:18] Marco Diaz: yep. we support SAML 2.0 for SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and OIDC as well. in Dedicated & Private you get a private control plane and can connect to your identity provider directly. Hosted supports SAML with enterprise plans; there's an onboarding flow and we can provide metadata files. we also support role mappings to groups so you can enforce RBAC.

[03:40] Evelyn Moore: do you support conditional access and MFA via SAML claims? also how is RBAC enforced — can we have per-team model access controls and audit trails?
[03:48] Marco Diaz: yes, conditional access policies are enforced via your IdP; redwood honors SAML assertion attributes and maps to RBAC roles. RBAC is enforced at the API/token level — you can have route-level controls, model-level permissions, and keys tied to teams. all actions are logged to audit events which can be exported.

[04:10] Raj Patel: legal question — retention of logs for e-discovery and audits, can you hold logs for 7 years? what's practical?
[04:17] Leah Kim: hi raj, from CSM, we typically see customers request 1-7 years; we can configure retention and integrate with your SIEM via log exporters. longer retention has storage/cost implications; we can provide rolling exports to your S3.

[04:35] Tom Nguyen: format of audit logs — are they structured JSON with actor, action, resource, timestamp? we need to ingest into our ELK.
[04:43] Marco Diaz: yes, JSON schema with fields: user_id, role, action, resource, model_version, request_id, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out. we'll attach the schema sample in the follow-up doc.

[05:00] [background crosstalk — phone beep]

[05:15] Evelyn Moore: can we redact PII in logs? some results could contain customer data.
[05:20] Marco Diaz: we support redaction pipelines — you can configure scrubbing rules and downstream exporters only get hashed or scrubbed outputs. for private deployment, you control the scrubbing pipeline.

[05:35] Priya Shah: data residency: we need data and logs to remain in eu-west-1. is that supported in Hosted?
[05:42] Marco Diaz: hosted has region-specific endpoints; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control the region and VPC. Hosted enterprise can pin data regionally, but dedicated offers firmer contractual guarantees.

[06:05] Tom Nguyen: ok — cost/latency tradeoff: we expect steady 200 token/sec per app with spikes to 1k. what's your recommended mode?
[06:15] Marco Diaz: Dedicated if you need predictable tail latency and throughput; Hosted is fine for more elastic workloads. we also provide intelligent batching and auto-scaling — redwood optimize suggests quantization and batching profiles to reduce token costs. for steady high throughput with tight SLOs, Dedicated or Private.

[06:40] Jasmine Patel: objection often: customers worry about vendor lock-in — are model artifacts portable?

[06:45] Marco Diaz: we support model versioning and you can pin to open models; we provide tooling to export model artifacts and KV caches where applicable. for private deployments there's full access to the runtime.

[07:00] Evelyn Moore: about SOC2 evidence — do you provide the full report or a consented summary? we have to present to our board.

[07:08] Leah Kim: we provide SOC2 Type II attestation and a short summary; we can also arrange a security questionnaire response. certain raw reports are shared under NDA.

[07:22] Raj Patel: any pen tests or third-party audits?

[07:26] Marco Diaz: yes, annual pen tests and code security scans; we can share scope and remediation history in the follow-up.

[07:40] Tom Nguyen: networking — can you run in our private subnet with no public egress? we have strict network controls.

[07:48] Marco Diaz: Private supports fully air-gapped/on-prem installs and VPC-only control plane. Dedicated can be VPC peered with restricted egress and firewall rules; we'll share the network checklist.

[08:05] Priya Shah: for keys — rotation and revocation. if we revoke a key, do you have a process to force re-encryption / fail-closed?

[08:15] Marco Diaz: yes, we support key rotation workflows and can force rekeying on startup. failing closed is an option — requests will fail until new key is provisioned. we'll include runbooks.

[08:30] [00:09:30 marker] Jasmine Patel: let's talk about RBAC granularity — maps to org/team/service accounts?

[08:40] Marco Diaz: we map roles to groups and service accounts; you can set per-model, per-route permissions, and key-scoped usage. we also support token-level quotas for teams.

[09:00] Evelyn Moore: data processing agreement and processor controls — do you sign standard DPAs?

[09:07] Jasmine Patel: yes, DPA and standard EU SCCs available; legal can share redlines. raj?

[09:12] Raj Patel: we'll review, but want to see indemnity clauses for data breaches.

[09:20] Marco Diaz: we'll route legal questions; redwood has standard enterprise contracting for such cases.

[09:35] Priya Shah: logs export — can we stream to our SIEM in near-real-time? what about throughput limits?

[09:42] Marco Diaz: yes, near-real-time export to your S3/Kafka/Splunk with backpressure handling. throughput scales with plan; we'll include examples.

[10:00] Tom Nguyen: curious re: model KV cache security — if cached prefixes are sensitive, how is that protected?

[10:08] Marco Diaz: KV cache is encrypted at rest with CMK and is scoped per-tenant in Dedicated/Private. access control enforced by runtime. we can provide an architecture diagram for cache isolation.

[10:30] [slight transcription glitch — speaker label wrong below]
[10:35] Speaker 1: uh yeah um can you also show us a cost comparison example for 100M tokens/mo?
[10:40] Jasmine Patel: good call — i'll follow up with comps for Hosted vs Dedicated including burst and storage costs.

[10:55] Evelyn Moore: any regulatory compliance beyond SOC2 — HIPAA, PCI?
[11:02] Marco Diaz: we have customers in healthcare; private deployments used for HIPAA workloads. PCI depends on scope — we can discuss segmentation and attestation approaches.

[11:20] Priya Shah: onboarding timeline — how long to stand up Dedicated in our account?

[11:26] Marco Diaz: typically 2-6 weeks depending on capacity and networking approvals. private on-prem can be longer (4-12 weeks).

[11:40] Tom Nguyen: ok. let's talk about the bench — what's the expected run and outputs?

[11:45] Marco Diaz: we'll propose a 2-hour bench: your sample traffic, run Hosted (if possible) and Dedicated test cluster with your KMS integration, capture tail latency p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll also test prefix caching effectiveness. deliverable: benchmark report + raw traces.

[12:10] Priya Shah: do you allow us to run a synthetic workload that includes PII to validate scrubbing? any restrictions?

[12:18] Marco Diaz: for privacy, we recommend using masked PII or a contracted data handling process; for private deployment you can use real data within your network. we'll add options in the bench plan.

[12:35] Jasmine Patel: quick note — we'll attach the SOC2 cert, the network checklist, sample audit log schema, and a bench plan to the follow-up email.

[12:48] Raj Patel: provisioning of support — SLA and escalation path?

[12:53] Leah Kim: enterprise SLA tiers available; 24/7 support for P1s, named contacts, and quarterly reviews.

[13:05] Evelyn Moore: final question from me — encryption key escrow or split-key options?

[13:12] Marco Diaz: we have HSM integrations and can support split-key patterns as part of an advanced deployment. we'll include options and tradeoffs.

[13:30] Jasmine Patel: alright, recap and next steps.

Recap (approx):
- Silverpine needs SOC2 attestation, customer-managed KMS, SAML/SCIM, RBAC per team, long-term audit retention options, and regionally pinned deployments.
- Action items: redwood to share SOC2 artifacts, private deployment diagram, audit log schema, benchmark plan and pricing comps.
- Bench: dedicated test cluster run with KMS integration and cache tests.

[14:26] Tom Nguyen: thanks, look forward to the bench.
